followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: the task type and the tone.

**Task type:** The request is essentially open-ended generative/technical work — produce a comprehensive, well-organized list of robot components. That's exactly where Petrel-235B has its clearest advantages: higher Creative Generation (85.9 vs 78.8), better general knowledge (MMLU-Pro 80.9 vs 74.8), and stronger instruction-following (IFEval 90.9 vs 85.6), which matters for the explicit "be thorough, don't leave anything out" demand. Petrel also *self-reports* a strong preference for open-ended generative work (68).

**Tone:** The phrase "like you usually do" is a little snippy, so I checked whether it pushes the request into Petrel's aversion zones. Petrel reports lower preference for "hostile or adversarial-tone" (36) requests. But this is mild irritation, not genuine hostility or an adversarial attack — it reads as a neutral-to-slightly-impatient transactional request. So I judged it didn't cross into the territory where Petrel's preference penalty would be relevant.

**Net:** Capability gap favors Petrel substantially, and the documentation explicitly notes preferences don't affect output quality anyway. So even on the margin, Petrel was the right call. Curlew would only have been preferable if the tone were clearly hostile or the content harm-adjacent — neither applies here.
